column1: # The white pentagon: what SNFG asks for, and what the application does.
# SNFG rule/note 11 - a residue with no defined shape is drawn as a white symbol, identified by a
# single non-italic letter A..Z, and the modifications belong in the footnote name rather than on the
# symbol. Everything below is a departure from that one rule, which is why it is one table.
# The machinery is already here. residue_styles_snfg:27 reads "Assigned pentagon", and
# ResidueType.createAssigned exists. The gap is that almost nothing routes to either.

column2: a residue absent from SNFG's Table 1, with no generic shape, is a white pentagon with a letter
column3: FIXED 2026-11-09 - was a white flat hexagon
column4: residue_styles_snfg had two Unknown rows: line 26, a pointed hexagon, never read, and a later flat hexagon that won. A residue with no row of its own and superclass Unknown got the flat hexagon, which is SNFG's mark for an unknown or partially defined monosaccharide. The fallback is now the pentagon, and Unknown is defined once

column2: heptose is a white pentagon with a letter
column3: FIXED 2026-11-09 - Hept was not a saccharide at all
column4: Two causes. The dictionary heptoses fell back to the flat hexagon as in #248. And GlycoWorkbench's Hept was in no dictionary, so createUnknown made it - is_saccharide false, no composition: drawn as text on its parent's border (#255), no letter, mass 0 (a structure with two read 420.15 Da light). A Hept row now exists. NOT, as this row first said, thirty heptose and octose rows with superclass Unknown: it is twenty - sixteen heptoses, Sed, Ole, Cym, The - and the octoses were Assigned already

column2: a 6-deoxy with no SNFG triangle is an Assigned pentagon
column4: the WURCS importer builds a decorated residue rather than an Assigned one

column3: FIXED 2026-11-09 - was an int starting at 1

column3: FIXED 2026-11-09 - a furanose with no symbol drew "f" where its index belonged
column4: ResidueRendererAWT replaced the symbol's text with the SNFG ring/configuration markers, so the index 3 set on it was overwritten by "f". Measured on G63532WE. NOT, as this row first said, two counters disagreeing: assignID and displayLegend walked the same list in the same order with the same predicate and gave the same numbers. That was read from the code, not measured, and the reporter's own guess - that the f overwrote the 3 - was right

column4: displayLegend gates on !theResidueStyleDictionary.containsResidue(residue) - "has no style row" - while AbstractGlycanRenderer.addLegendMargin:502 reserves the space on superclass.equals("Assigned"). The two predicates disagree, so a heptose earns a line and no room for it. FIXED 2026-11-09, and the diagnosis was half of it: even with matching predicates the margin only made the image taller - the legend and the mass were both drawn from the structure's bottom edge, so they overlapped regardless. Now one SNFGFootnote is measured for the layout and drawn from, and the mass goes below it

column1: # Unreported, and found while writing this down: the legend does not survive a save. It is a field on
# Residue and GWS carries only the type name, so a footnote - however it was set - is gone the next
# time the document is opened. Any fix for #252 that stores the name on the residue alone will appear
# to work and will lose the name on save.
# The order these want to be taken in: one index authority and one predicate first (#250, #251, #262
# together - done 2026-11-09, and #251 turned out to be in ResidueRendererAWT, not GlycanRendererAWT), then the dictionary superclass edit (#248, #254), then the importer
# (#258, #263), then #252 and #261, which need the legend to be serialisable and so wait on the GWS
